title.title: The simplex has the largest isotropic constant
title.subtitle: Claim: in every dimension, $L_K$ is at most the simplex’s value, with equality only for simplices

plain: Among solid shapes of equal volume, which is the most spread out? The claim: the simplex, a triangle in 2D

panels.axisLabel: the isotropic constant $L_K$ in the plane

beats.text: A disc, a square and a triangle, each of area 1, centred at their centroids
Their isotropic constants, computed exactly: the triangle’s is the largest
Claim: in every dimension the simplex has the largest $L_K$, and only the simplex

steps: Restate the question as an entropy inequality for random laws
Transport a Gaussian onto the law, coordinate by coordinate
Higher-order chaos terms give a spectral gap that closes it

achievement.label: The sharp simplex conjecture for isotropic constants
achievement.context: Before: $L_K$ bounded (Klartag–Lehec, 2024); the sharp form known in the plane
achievement.note: If right, it also implies the general Mahler inequality (Klartag, 2018)

verify.detail: No Lean: 42 pages of hard analysis, unformalized. Treat it as a claim
verify.ourCheck: We read the paper and abstract; nothing here is machine-checked

voice.text: A disk, a square, a triangle of equal area. Computed exactly, the triangle spreads most.
Restate it as entropy, transport a Gaussian, and use a spectral gap.
Claimed: the simplex, in every dimension.

sources.quote: L_K <= (n!)^{1/n} / ((n+1)^{(n+1)/(2n)} sqrt(n+2)), the isotropic constant of the simplex, with equality iff K is a simplex
Bourgain's slicing problem (L_K bounded by an absolute constant) was resolved by Klartag and Lehec (arXiv:2412.15044, Dec 2024
proved in the plane by Campi-Colesanti-Gronchi
Klartag (Adv. Math. 2018) showed the simplex bound implies nonsymmetric Mahler.
Unformalized and not peer-reviewed, 42 pages of hard analysis
